terms.gloss: a child’s own money: pocket money
evidence: Liv. 2.41.10: pecūliumque fīliī, and the son’s own money
Plaut. Asin. 498: nec potest pecūlium ēnumerārī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What a Roman father let his son, or a master his slave, hold and spend as his own (Lewis & Short); also his savings (see save, money).

evidence: Cic. Att. 15.15.4: quod sit in annuum sūmptum eī, what he needs for his year’s allowance
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for his son’s allowance as a student at Athens; properly expense (see spend, money).

phrases.latin: quā rē velim cūrēs (nec tibi essem molestus, sī per alium hoc agere possem) ut permūtētur Athēnās quod sit in annuum sūmptum eī
phrases.english: so please see to it (I would not trouble you if I could do it through anyone else) that his allowance for the year is sent to Athens by bill of exchange

phrases.latin: Ecce tibi pecūlium; nummōs in loculōs dēmitte.
phrases.english: Here’s your pocket money; drop the coins in your money box.

sources: Lewis & Short: peculium · Lewis & Short: sumptus
